## Anomaly
{"kind": "broken_link", "system": "verification", "title": "No feature_verified_<id> counters despite checks passing", "expected": "Each passing feature bumps its feature_verified_<id> counter to exactly 1, with FeatureVerified_<id> set.", "observed": "Round 1 shows checks_passed=11 and purchase_live_check_pass=1, but no feature_verified_* counter appears anywhere in the counters.", "severity": "medium"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The server half of the feature verifier does not exist. FeatureChecksConfig defines the feature_verified_<id> counter names and the FeatureVerifyReq/FeatureVerifyRes remotes. FeatureVerifyClient waits up to 10s for ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.FeatureVerifyReq/Res and exits silently when they never appear. Its header comment says the counters are bumped by the server verifier when it gets the client's replies. No server script creates those remotes, sends requests, or calls Telemetry.count on the feature_verified_* counters. ForgeTelemetry is a no-op on the client, so nothing else can bump them. The live playtest confirms this: ReplicatedStorage.Remotes holds only RebirthRequest and RebirthResult. A source search of all scripts found only FeatureVerifyClient and FeatureChecksConfig referencing the verifier. The counters therefore never appear even though checks_passed=11 and purchase_live_check_pass=1. This is a game bug: a missing server-side verifier service. Game.server.luau never starts one.", "file": "ServerScriptService/Game.server.luau", "evidence": "Server probe: Remotes folder children = [RebirthRequest, RebirthResult] only, with no FeatureVerifyReq or FeatureVerifyRes. Counters contain no feature_verified_*. Source search over all LuaSourceContainers for 'FeatureChecksConfig', 'feature_verified' or 'FeatureVerify' matched only StarterPlayerScripts/FeatureVerifyClient and ReplicatedStorage/FeatureChecksConfig. ## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().
